eps.d: Pete has given up his job in advertising to concentrate on writing, and he and his family have to move to a less salubrious district. They discover their house is already occupied - by a Jewish ghost.
Pete tells Sally if you ignore ghosts they go away. Try telling that to Yetta Feldman.
Pete has a deadline to meet - but all he keeps meeting is a dead lady.
When Pete faces the spectre of unemployment, Sally turns to the spectre in their house.
A visit from a friend of Pete's has a surprising effect on Sally.
If Yetta's long-lost daughter can be found, maybe everyone can rest in peace...
Pete's new client is taking over the family. But isn't that what Yetta'stheretodo?
When Pete's parents arrive from Manchester, Yetta meets her match.
A mid-life crisis is bad - but a mid-death crisis can be murder...
When Pete lets his home be used for a commercial he hasn't reckoned on "Yetta Garbo".
Heaven knows how the Rokebys can get rid of Yetta. But is heaven telling?
When a ghost feels useless, it's time for some serious haunting...
Yetta is forced to make a choice between this world and the next as she confronts a life-and-death dilemma.
The Rokeby's have their new lives all planned out - but the best laid plans...
Sally goes into counselling mode, while Pete becomes a star ad-man.
When Pete's widowed mother comes to stay and brings her fiance, even Yetta gets a fright.
When the inspector calls, the spectre takes over the case.
In the last of the series, Yetta is dying to go to a wedding.
